pr_comments:
Make sure to test thoroughly as IIRC this convoluted connect/disconnect logic was to enable reusing the same dialog for both the "Create New Script" and "Attach Script" functions.

If both seem to work fine, that's all good.

Ah damn, you are right, this requires more testing. It seems that I did not see the getter used to retrieve the script_create_dialog variable. So I assumed it could not be used elsewhere... I don't see why we need to reuse the same dialog though, maybe another one might be created I guess.

That being said, it also looks like this vairiable is expose via get_script_create_dialog() into EditorPlugin. I don't really see the point there, maybe it's used somewhere to add something? That's really weird...

Alright, I updated the PR with a simpler fix. It would be good to someday refactor all of this but it needs more work.
I believe that if the ScriptEditorDialog has to be shared, it should likely be moved into EditorNode, instead of the scene tree dock.

issue_context.title: Attempt to connect nonexistent signal 'popup_hide' to 'SceneTreeDock::_script_creation_closed'.
issue_context.body:
**Godot version:**
4.0.dev.custom_build. 1957c99ab
**OS/device including version:**
Ubuntu 19.10
**Issue description:**

```
ERROR: Signal 'script_created' is already connected to given callable 'SceneTreeDock::_script_created' in that object.
   at: connect (core/object.cpp:1462)
ERROR: In Object of type 'ScriptCreateDialog': Attempt to connect nonexistent signal 'popup_hide' to callable 'SceneTreeDock::_script_creation_closed'.
   at: connect (core/object.cpp:1449)

```
**Steps to reproduce:**
![jfile](https://user-images.githubusercontent.com/41945903/78453952-4222c100-7695-11ea-87fe-5689c10c57b3.gif)
comments:
Still reproducible in current `master` branch.

`ScriptCreateDialog` inherits `ConfirmationDialog`, and dialogs now inherit `Window` directly and no longer `Popup`, so they don't have `popup_hide`.

Instead they have `confirmed` and `cancelled`, but overall the logic used to connect a specific signal only when using the dialog in "Attach Script" mode, to disconnect it on close, is a bit messy. So some cleanup of this logic would be welcome.

review_comments: Are you sure that this one is unnecessary? I assume it was put here to reset things which might have been modified in the Create New Script variant of this dialog.

This only thing it did was to disconnect the "script_created" signal. I believe this was added originally only to avoid the "signal already connected" message, because I see no other reason to disconnect this signal otherwise.

Since now the signal connection is done once and not every time the attach_script_to_selected function is ran, I see no reason to keep this.
